The list's address-block County code was never read (only its column name, in the header listing); that is why candidates are placed through the supervisors' pages, and it stays John's call. Tool output showed: column names, counts, office headings, and name, party and status for 13 contests checked against the sources. Twice it also showed the Division of Elections' own office address and phone from a page footer (a government office, not a person). The supervisors' pages carry campaign money figures; those and their links were never kept. lessons: Florida's local candidate download names an office and seat but no county or district (its only county code sits in the candidate's address block and is not read), so state_local_fl.py places each row by finding the same name, office and seat on the county supervisor's candidate page (voterfocus.com/CampaignFinance/candidate_pr.php?c=<county>, one layout for all 67) and takes the contests and district names from the Secretary of State's 67 Notices of General Election PDFs on dos.fl.gov.

In that download 'Unopposed' also covers a candidate who won outright on August 18 (the rivals read 'Defeated'), accented letters are Windows-1252 bytes rather than UTF-8, and a supervisor's page can lag behind (still 'Qualified' after a defeat), so the Division's status decides who is on the ballot and any disagreement goes in a note or a gap.
